description:
## Problem

Reach detects manual Path.basename/URI.parse bypasses (String.split("/") |> List.last instead of Path.basename). These are security-relevant because hand-rolled path parsing often misses edge cases like path traversal sequences.

## Evidence

From reach/lib/reach/evidence/standard_library_bypass/path_uri.ex:
- manual_path_basename: String.split("/") |> List.last instead of Path.basename
- manual_path_extension: String.split(".") |> List.last instead of Path.extname
- manual_uri_path_split: String.split("?") |> List.first instead of URI.parse
- manual_query_parsing: String.split("&") instead of URI.decode_query
- manual_uri_scheme_split: String.split("://") instead of URI.parse

## Expected Behavior

These patterns should be detected as security code smells — hand-rolled path/URL parsing is a common source of path traversal and SSRF vulnerabilities.

## Suggested Fix

This is a code smell check, not a taint-based security rule. Consider adding to the AI linter or Claws:
- Detect String.split("/") |> List.last → suggest Path.basename
- Detect String.split(".") |> List.last → suggest Path.extname
- Detect String.split("?") |> List.first → suggest URI.parse

This is lower priority than the taint-engine fixes but would catch real security anti-patterns.
title: Elixir: detect manual Path/URI bypasses as security code smells
